work.title: On the End Times

paragraphs.text: Again: On the Last Times, by Mar Isaac. Truth jolted me; it called to me as to someone asleep and awakened me, teaching me about the coming of the last times. It became my teacher, and I was like a disciple listening to its words. My thoughts were filled with the teaching of the herald of life. I heard from it voices proclaiming the resurrection, and the mystery that says, “Peace henceforth upon the righteous.” “Incline your ear, young man, and listen,” it said to me. “Run and proclaim everything I tell you to anyone who will listen to you. Open your mouth to me, child, and I will fill it with a sweet spring: words much sweeter than honey to those who hear them. Instead of a whip. Come, be scourged by the reports; instead of a rod, let the news of the decrees discipline you. If you understand the meaning of the Scriptures—or if not, ask—the end has arrived. The prophets cry out, and so do the apostles. Nature itself also teaches you through its laws: its adornments have come to an end, as have its furnishings, together with its [?]. Look at your years and your days, and examine yourself. Wickedness has become king; save your neck from its injuries. An evil king has taken power on earth, and now he throws it into turmoil. Take refuge in the King on high, and he will rescue you. Satan and his servants thirst for the soul’s blood. It is a calamity if you fall into his hands, for he will kill you. He kills more in inhabited places than in the wilderness—woe to those he kills! In the desert he leads people into sin more than in inhabited places. Where will you flee? For he strangles those in inhabited places with desire, and those in the mountains with hateful anxiety and worry. If you enter an inhabited place, the dreadful wilderness is better than it; if you go out into the desert, your heart bursts from the terrors. For the whole earth has been corrupted, thrown into turmoil by the wicked. There is fear in inhabited places, and in the desert there are terrors as well. Sins in the wilderness, jealousy in inhabited places, injustice everywhere! Truth is oppressed, and faithfulness is hard for its seekers to find. The world has grown old, and the flavor of its youth has faded. It stands in fear at the mouth of the grave, and now it is departing. The earth has grown weary, and its strength has dwindled because of acts of pride. It is time for it to rest and be freed from labor. The way of truth has been forgotten by many. Everyone has trodden a path of his own and gone astray. Creation has debased itself like a [?] prostitute. It has committed adultery in wickedness and betrothed itself to wantonness. A wind, which is sin, has blown over the sea of injustice. Now the wicked have steered their ships toward Gehenna. Proudly they go, sinning, toward the pit of fire, and their hearts do not grieve over their sins with bitter weeping. A star of darkness has become their signpost on the road to death. Those who have abandoned the way of life travel toward it. Look, the sea is in turmoil, and the dry land is in uproar with their inhabitants. Everyone strives to see who can act more wickedly than his neighbor. I saw an evil man blaming another evil man for his deeds, and a sinner judging his companion for his wrongdoing. I sat in astonishment, put my hand to my cheek, and wept, because a wicked man’s companion accused him of his vile deeds. I saw an adulterer reproaching his companion for adultery, and an unclean man saying, “Oh, those unclean people who have practiced deceit!” And where is your heart, O accuser who has not accused himself? If justice is shown to you, you too are hateful. Look, your companion’s sin distresses you, you who show favoritism; your own wrongdoing does not rebuke you, you false judge. Do not let reports trouble you so that you cause your soul to sin through them. It is fitting for you to be accused rather than an accuser. Be willingly deaf and mute and without eyes: hear and remain quiet, see and keep silent, know and remain calm. Let this discernment be yours, so that it may justify you: first judge yourself within yourself, as is fitting for you. Speak peace concerning every person, like someone discerning; and through your humility be a friend rather than an enemy. Let the seal of silence be carefully set upon your mouth, and discipline with silence the slanderer who disturbs you. Sit and examine your land, the world, like a seer. See that all of it is full of perversity, and guard your conduct. There is no one innocent or free from evils, for everyone, according to his strength, is laden with them and carries sins. In the seventh year they granted slaves freedom. In the seventh millennium, set us free, Son of the Lord of all. In the seventh year the land rested, and orphans ate its produce. In the seventh millennium, give to the children from your grace. There was remission for all debtors in the seventh year. Grant forgiveness to all who have sinned in the seventh millennium. On the Sabbath there was rest for the people, for slaves and free people. On your Sabbath, our Lord, let there be forgiveness for the good and the wicked. Mix [?] with your exposition, and deeds as well. Reduce words and increase labors together with victories. Do not be a river that is full, foul, and muddy. Be a spring that trickles a little and tastes sweet. The discourse on the last times, by Mar Isaac, is finished.
